Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-03-15
- Start: 14:00 PT
- Duration: ~47 minutes
- Attendees: Alice Nguyen (Redwood AE), Marco Silva (Redwood SE), Dana Ortiz (CTO, Resin), Liam Chen (Head of ML, Resin), Priya Rao (Infra Eng, Resin)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Purpose: map Resin's expected token volume, understand latency SLAs, and evaluate which deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) makes sense given budget constraints.
- Key asks: per-token/unit economics, batching and KV cache impacts, private/VPC options and SOC2/KMS questions, pilot timeline and benchmark plan.

Topics: pricing per token, batching strategies, KV cache benefits, autoscaling, private deployment constraints, security/SOC2, timeline for pilot.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alice (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, we got about 45 minutes, want to make sure we cover cost model and a quick mapping to deploy modes. dana you mentioned token volumes in the invite?
[00:12] Dana (Resin CTO): yeah thanks Alice, um, we have a chat assistant and a summarization pipeline — peak concurrency is around 1200 rps but typical is 200 to 400, token distribution is heavy on context windows, average request 1.4k input tokens, 350 output tokens. those numbers are pretty rough.
[00:30] Liam (Head of ML): and to add, we sometimes have long multi-turn threads so KV cache effectiveness is a big question for us. we want to avoid re-sending 800 tokens every time if possible.
[00:44] Marco (Redwood SE): right, so two levers—prefix caching (KV cache) and batching. caching helps when you have repeated prefixes or multi-turn, batching helps on throughput. quick Q: what's your 95th percentile latency target?
[00:58] Priya (Infra Eng): for customer-facing chat we need sub-400ms for 95p ideally, but we can trade some of that to 600ms during peaks if cost savings are significant.
[01:12] Alice: good, that's helpful. for cost context, our hosted per-token list rates vary by model family but to ballpark — some large open families often end up in low single-digit tenths of a cent per 1k tokens after discounts, but precise number depends on model size, quantization, and batching. i realize that's vague, we'll give concrete sheet.
[01:34] Dana: yeah concrete numbers would be great. also curious about Dedicated — if we reserve capacity what kind of unit economics change?
[01:44] Marco: Dedicated reduces per-token inference cost significantly because you pay a reserved GPU pool and get predictable throughput. for workloads like yours with sustained concurrency, Dedicated often wins on raw token cost — directional example: hosted might be Xc/token, dedicated reduces variable cost by 30-60% depending on utilization and model.
[02:05] Liam: can you explain that utilization caveat — we have diurnal spikes; we don't want to overcommit.
[02:12] Marco: absolutely. Dedicated is best when utilization is high; we model effective cost by amortizing reserved capacity across expected utilization. we also have burst and autoscale policies so you don't have to provision for absolute peaks. but if you have wide spikes and low base, hosted hybrid can be better.
[02:28] [00:02:30] Priya: what about KV "cash" — sorry KV cache — is that available across Hosted and Private equally? are there cross-tenant concerns?
[02:39] Marco: bit of nuance: KV cache is supported in the runtime across modes. for Hosted we use isolation policies and TLS for in-transit, but caching layers are per-tenant and encrypted; for Private/VPC you control the cache placement. there's also a performance delta: on Dedicated/Private there is lower network jitter and you can colocate cache nearer to model for better hit latency.
[02:58] Dana: any ballpark for token savings from caching? in our multi-turn threads i suspect 30-50% of tokens are repeat context.
[03:06] Marco: yes we typically see 20-60% effective token reduction depending on app pattern. the caveat is you need stable prefixes; if prompts change a lot the hit rate falls. we'll want to see a histogram of your token reuse.
[03:20] [00:03:20] Liam: ok we'll share traces. another thing — quantization and model variants. are there recommended families that strike the best balance for us?
[03:30] Marco: generally for summarization and chat you can often move to an int8 or 4-bit quantized variant with a small quality delta; that reduces GPU runtime cost by up to 40% in some cases. we can run evals on your prompts to measure quality/regressions.
[03:46] Dana: and legal/security — we require SOC2 and customer audit logs, SSO, and keys in our KMS, do you guys support that on Hosted?
[03:56] Alice: short answer yes for enterprise tiers — hosted enterprise comes with SOC2, SAML/SSO, audit logs export, and we can integrate with customer KMS for private or dedicated customers; for fully private (on-prem) you retain full KMS control. we'll attach the security packet.
[04:12] [00:04:12] Priya: on network egress and data residency — some EU customers require data stay in region, is regional deployment available?
[04:19] Alice: yes we have region routing and can pin to regions; Private deployments give you the most control for strict residency.
[04:26] Liam: okay back to costs — can you walk through an example calculation? say 1M monthly active requests with average tokens you mentioned.
[04:36] Marco: sure quick rough calc: at 1M requests * (1.4k input + 350 output) ~= 1.75B tokens. if hosted blended rate is e.g., $0.0009 per token, that's about $1.575M monthly — obviously that number is illustrative. with Dedicated and good utilization you could bring variable cost down 30-50% plus reserved fee amortized.
[05:00] Dana: wow that seems high — can you get to sub-$0.8M?
[05:05] Marco: possibly with aggressive caching and quantization. if caching reduces tokens by 40% and you use a quantized model that's 40% lower runtime per token you'd see big savings: 1.75B * 0.6 * $0.0005 ~= $525k plus base reserved fees. again many moving parts.
[05:26] [00:05:26] Speaker 4: I think the math checks but we need the worksheet.
[05:30] Alice: yep we'll send a tailored worksheet with columns for: raw tokens, cache-hit-adjusted tokens, model variant cost, reserved capacity amortization, and burst costs.
[05:40] Priya: do you support prefix-level caching eviction policies? we need TTL and per-customer segmentation.
[05:47] Marco: yes, TTL and per-tenant namespaces, plus we support LRU and size-based policies. for Private you can tune the cache instances.
[05:58] [00:05:58] Liam: question on concurrency — if we hit 1200 rps at peak how does batching affect latency?
[06:06] Marco: batching improves throughput but increases tail latency for individual requests if you wait to fill a batch. our runtime uses adaptive batching with latency SLO awareness — it will not wait beyond configured time window for latency-critical routes. you can set per-route latency SLOs so chat remains low-latency and background summarization can be batched aggressively.
[06:28] Dana: do you have empirical numbers? like at 1200 rps what's expected p95 for 1k-token outputs?
[06:35] Marco: depends on GPU and model, but on Dedicated with A100-like hardware and optimized kernels you might see ~200-300ms for p50 and 350-500ms p95 for ~1k output tokens with caching; hosted is a bit higher due to multi-tenant jitter. we'll provide bench numbers from similar customers.
[06:53] [00:06:53] Liam: what's the rollback/fallback story if the model goes bad or overloaded?
[07:00] Alice: we have routing policies: automatic fallback to smaller model variants, regional fallback, and queued/buffered responses. also canary rollouts and instant rollbacks. important for SLA.
[07:10] Dana: are there egress costs or hidden fees for embedding storage or logs?
[07:16] Alice: logs and observability are in tiers — basic logs included, extended retention is an add-on. no hidden per-embedding storage fees in Hosted beyond usage; we'll lay out line items.
[07:26] [00:07:26] Priya: operationally who handles model upgrades and quantization testing?
[07:32] Marco: Redwood's model ops team manages runtime variants; for Dedicated/Private we partner with your team on scheduled upgrades and provide test harnesses. we recommend a canary bucket of traffic to validate.
[07:44] Dana: timeline — we want a pilot in 6 weeks if possible, with a production decision by quarter end. feasible?
[07:50] Alice: yes—pilot flows look like: 1) share traces + success criteria (you) 2) we propose pilot config and pricing (us) 3) run 2-4 week pilot with benchmarks and quality evals 4) review and decide. that aligns with 6 weeks if traces are shared quickly.
[08:08] [00:08:08] Liam: for the pilot, do you need full traffic or can we sample? we worry about pre-production data differences.
[08:15] Marco: sample traces are fine for initial bench; for end-to-end we prefer a production-similar load. we have traffic replay tooling.
[08:24] Dana: security paperwork? we need an initial security questionnaire filled before pilot.
[08:29] Alice: we'll attach our security packet and can complete an initial questionnaire; for enterprise we'll do a SOC2 attestation and potential on-site audit if needed.
[08:40] [00:08:40] Speaker 2: (inaudible) i had a question on spot vs reserved GPU pricing...
[08:45] Marco: spot helps on Dedicated as a way to reduce costs for non-critical batch jobs; reserved is for production. you can mix.
[08:52] Priya: SLA — what's uptime for Dedicated?
[08:55] Alice: Dedicated comes with SLA depending on commitment tier, common is 99.9% with credits for breaches; Hosted enterprise has similar SLA with multi-region failover.
[09:05] [00:09:05] Liam: how do you attribute token accounting — do you charge on input+output or just output?
[09:11] Alice: we bill on total tokens processed, input + output, since both consume compute. some customers model charges differently internally but external billing is total tokens.
[09:20] Dana: can we set per-route cost caps to avoid surprise bills?
[09:24] Marco: yes we have quota and budget controls per API key/route and alerts when thresholds approached. you can also enforce hard cutoffs.
[09:33] [00:09:33] Priya: for Private/on-prem, licensing model? is it a flat platform fee plus support?
[09:40] Alice: Private is typically a platform license + support + optional managed services. pricing is based on expected capacity and support level.
[09:48] Liam: competitor landscape — we've been evaluating Anthropic and some self-host options; curious how Redwood differentiates on economics.
[09:56] Marco: main differentiators: runtime optimization for higher utilization (better kernels, batching), integrated caching, and operational tooling that reduces friction and hidden costs. plus consistent deployment modes so you can start hosted and move to Private seamlessly.
[10:12] [00:10:12] Dana: one more practical — can you add an example of a billing line-item for a route that does 200k monthly calls with our average tokens?
[10:20] Alice: yes that's part of the worksheet. we'll include per-route examples, and sensitivity analysis for caching hit rates and quantization.
[10:30] Marco: also want to flag quality regressions — moving to a quantized model might change outputs; we run automatic evals against your prompt set and surface any regressions with examples.
[10:44] Dana: good. if quality dips more than our threshold we want automatic fallback to a higher-fidelity variant.
[10:50] Marco: supported — route-level fallback policies exist.
[10:54] [00:10:54] Priya: any constraints on open-source model licensing for Dedicated/Private?
[10:59] Marco: we can host any license-compatible model; for some L4 licenses we advise legal review; for private you manage model licensing.
[11:08] Dana: ok near the end — can you summarize exactly what you'll send and what we need to provide?
[11:15] Alice: sure — we'll send: 1) pricing worksheet with worked examples, 2) latency/benchmark deck from comparable deployments, 3) security packet (SOC2, SSO/KMS docs), 4) pilot proposal and sample test plan. we need from you: traces/histograms of token lengths and reuse, success criteria for latency and quality, and a contact for infra to coordinate pilot.
[11:41] Marco: i'll also propose a tech deep dive focused on KV cache tuning, autoscaling policies, and quantization regressions; that'll be more hands-on — 90 minutes.
[11:53] [00:11:53] Dana: sounds good. thanks. quick note — pricing needs to be granular; execs want worst-case and best-case numbers.
[11:59] Alice: we'll provide low/likely/high buckets.
[12:03] Dana: ok 1 more thing — can you show us example math for when Dedicated breaks even vs Hosted?
[12:09] Marco: yes, that's standard in the worksheet: break-even line as a function of sustained qps and utilization percent.
[12:17] [00:12:17] Liam: final Q — who is our TAM/AE escalation?
[12:22] Alice: I'm your AE; Marco is the SE. i'll be point for pricing and contract, marco for tech.
[12:29] Alice: thanks everyone for your time, we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites.
